refuted.verdict: OVER-READ, and it is the same class of error the day is auditing.
evidence: chron_spine_gate.py has ZERO scheduled callers. Verified across all four scheduler surfaces: hermes cron jobs.json (0 refs), crontab -l (0), /etc/cron.d (0 files), systemd units (0). The only reference anywhere on the box is /root/AAA/scripts/seal_chron_day.py:53 — my own daily record script, which merely HASHES the file. It never executes it.
The 14:00 job does not run the gate. It runs a 3,550-character LLM PROMPT that names chron.py and the SKILL.md under an 'evidence:' header — as reading matter, not as an executable check.

The gate's own selftest() exercises only b1, b2, b5 (re-derived: boundary refs inside selftest are ['b1','b2','b5']), with 6 references to private paraphrase helpers (_b2_against, _b1_all_present, _b5_has_unbounded_prose) rather than the shipped checks. A parallel sweep found b4's probe never calls the real function — it hashes a temp file twice and asserts hashlib works.

The gate's PASS vocabulary is defined in its own header as 'the boundary holds on the artifact as it exists now' — a statement about the ARTIFACT, not about a runtime arrow. And its exit code cannot express UNBUILT: with 0 FAIL it returns 0, so UNBUILT and all-PASS are identical to any caller.
Per this day's own forged law: a gate that no door has is not a gate. These PASSes are declarations by an unexecuted script.
refuted.what_is_actually_true: Six boundaries currently hold BY INSPECTION of the artifacts they name, when the script is run by hand. That is a real and useful property — it is not the same as six runtime arrows having PASSED. Zero of the eleven runtime arrows (SCHEDULED -> ... -> RECEIPT_MATCHED) has been witnessed, because zero of the three ALPHA-ZEN jobs has ever fired.
refuted.consequence: The embryo framing is directionally right but its headline number borrows credibility from a script that never runs. Restate as: 6 of 9 boundary checks hold by inspection; 0 of 11 runtime arrows witnessed.

precision_on_enforced_claim_state.measured: The enforcement exists in exactly one place: chron_spine_gate.py b1, which returns FAIL if events lack source/confidence/target_date/audience. That is a genuine mechanism — hand-rolled, not schema-driven.
precision_on_enforced_claim_state.but: that mechanism sits in a script nothing invokes. In the LIVE delivery path, the 14:00 job is an LLM prompt; the claim-state discipline there is enforced by instruction-following, i.e. by the model's compliance, not by a mechanism.
precision_on_enforced_claim_state.so: claim-state is enforced OUTSIDE the delivery path and instructed INSIDE it. Precisely inverted from where enforcement is needed.

the_f13_binary.question: Does the daily card stay a briefing engine while the three learning arrows are built behind it, or does the card itself become the CHRON experiment surface?
the_f13_binary.recommendation: A — the card stays a briefing engine; the learning arrows are built behind it.
reasons: The card is on a live human path with ZERO witnessed runs. An unproven experiment on the human's daily surface spends attention that has not yet been earned.
'Keep the shell plastic; seal the causal spine.' The shell is the card. Making the shell the experiment surface welds the two together, which is the opposite of the doctrine.
It keeps the change reversible and the blast radius at zero — matching the standing constraint that nothing here should need new authority or touch production.
the_f13_binary.not_a_close_call: Option B would put an uncalibrated learner in the same object the human reads each day, before a single arrow is witnessed. That is a direction change with an irreversible-ish attention cost.
